title: Best trombone players and playing with fast company
summary: Robinson talks about trombonists in town and how playing with Harrison Bones and Chris Kelly's band improved him.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Well, who was the best trombone player then, Norfolk?

A real thunk trombone player, you know what I mean? Well, I tell you, at the time then, you see Dick, tell you the truth, them was more of a musical man, but good man, you understand? And they could play jazz too, you understand? But there was more musical man, you know? India was always good trombone players. Now they had to take like, they had Boris Fletcher right around there playing trombone. They had George Washington, Eddie Morris. Now all the people was playing more trombone when I was playing. They were all playing more than I was playing until, when I went back to my trombone again, I cut up with them fellas and I passed all them fellas. Because I got in fast company, you see? I got with Harrison Bones, Yank and all them fellas, Buddy Johnson, Eddie Vincent and all them fellas, fast fellas, you see? And I used to pay attention to what they were doing, you see? I don't know, that passed away. Now then, I was, fellas just gave me plenty of breaks too. Sometimes Harrison was going to let me play sometime, sometimes two jobs a week in this place. With Chris Keller Band, that band was more strong than what I was, but that band was pulling me, it was bringing me, you understand, you see? When you play with a bunch of throwing with you, that's pulling you, you see? It was more strong than me. But obviously we could throw in the band, but I got on the line good and got that trombone down like I wanted to. In other words, when you're on the trombone, you just can't throw everything that you figure that you want to do because you got to spot them something. You got to put some bad notes.
